intro: Excerpts copied from the live TubeScout source (C:\TUBESCOUT). Each shows the real code behind a capability and explains how it powers that feature. TubeScout hosts no LLM of its own — summarization, scoring and recommendation all route through NEXUS; YouTube is read-only; every pipeline stage degrades gracefully.

snippets.title: WAL connection with FK + busy-timeout
snippets.feature: Single SQLite store for channels, videos, summaries, scores
snippets.code:
def connect(db_path: str | None = None) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open a connection with WAL + foreign keys enabled."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(db_path or DB_PATH), timeout=10)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=8000")  # wait, don't error, on concurrent writers
    return conn
snippets.explanation: Every part of TubeScout opens its DB through this one helper. WAL lets the news page read while the sweep writes; foreign_keys=ON enforces the videos→channels / summaries→videos relationships; busy_timeout makes a concurrent writer wait rather than raise — important because the twice-daily cycle and the live page touch the same file. Row factory returns dict-like rows.

snippets.title: Idempotent schema migrations
snippets.feature: Schema evolves safely without a rebuild
snippets.explanation: init_db() runs the base CREATE TABLE script then this migrator on every startup. Each ALTER is guarded by a PRAGMA table_info check, so re-running is harmless. This is how favorites, manual-topic locks, channel-disable and the dedup columns were added after v1 shipped without ever dropping data.

snippets.title: Upsert that preserves manual overrides
snippets.feature: Re-syncing subscriptions never clobbers your tuning
snippets.code:
existing = conn.execute(
    "SELECT topic, priority FROM channels WHERE channel_id=?", (ch["channel_id"],)
).fetchone()
topic = ch.get("topic") or (existing["topic"] if existing else "other")
priority = ch.get("priority") or (existing["priority"] if existing else PRIORITY_DIGEST)
conn.execute("""
    INSERT INTO channels (channel_id, title, ..., topic, priority, subscribed, added_at)
    VALUES (:channel_id, :title, ..., :topic, :priority, 1, :added_at)
    ON CONFLICT(channel_id) DO UPDATE SET
        title=excluded.title,
        description=excluded.description,
        thumbnail=excluded.thumbnail,
        uploads_playlist=COALESCE(excluded.uploads_playlist, channels.uploads_playlist),
        subscribed=1
""", {...})
snippets.explanation: When pull_subscriptions re-reads your 816 subs, this upsert refreshes title/thumbnail but the ON CONFLICT clause deliberately does NOT touch topic or priority — so a channel you muted or moved stays muted/moved. uploads_playlist is COALESCE'd so a known playlist isn't wiped by a NULL from a partial fetch.

snippets.title: Read-only OAuth with auto-refresh
snippets.feature: Read your own subscriptions, change nothing
snippets.explanation: The only scope requested is youtube.readonly — TubeScout can read your subscriptions and uploads but can never post, like, or subscribe. A saved token is refreshed silently; a missing/expired token in a non-interactive run raises a clear instruction instead of crashing the cycle. The one-time browser login (--login) writes secrets/token.json, which is gitignored.

snippets.title: Quota-friendly upload reads
snippets.feature: Sweep 800+ channels inside the free tier
snippets.code:
resp = service.playlistItems().list(
    part="snippet,contentDetails",
    playlistId=uploads_playlist,
    maxResults=min(max_videos * 2, 50),
).execute()
videos = []
for item in resp.get("items", []):
    cd = item.get("contentDetails", {})
    pub_str = cd.get("videoPublishedAt") or item["snippet"].get("publishedAt")
    pub = datetime.fromisoformat(pub_str.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    if pub <= since:
        continue
    vid = cd.get("videoId") or item["snippet"].get("resourceId", {}).get("videoId")
    videos.append({"video_id": vid, "channel_id": item["snippet"].get("channelId"), ...})
    if len(videos) >= max_videos:
        break
return videos
snippets.explanation: Each channel's new uploads are read from its uploads playlist with playlistItems.list — 1 quota unit — instead of search.list which costs 100. Items published on/before the lookback cutoff are skipped. At 1 unit/channel × ~800 channels × 2 sweeps that's ~1,600 units against the 10,000/day free tier, with comfortable headroom.

snippets.title: App + CORS from the QI registry
snippets.feature: FastAPI news page + API any QI project can reach
snippets.code:
try:
    sys.path.insert(0, r"C:\QI\ECOSYSTEM")
    from qi_registry import QI
    _cors = QI.cors_origins()
except Exception:
    _cors = ["http://localhost:8503", "http://localhost:7843"]

app = FastAPI(
    title="TubeScout API",
    description="YouTube subscription intelligence ... — Quiddity Innovations",
    version="0.1.0"
)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=_cors,
                   allow_methods=["GET", "POST"], allow_headers=["*"])
snippets.explanation: The single FastAPI app on :8503 serving both the HTML pages and the JSON API. Allowed CORS origins come from the shared QI registry (with a localhost fallback) so sibling projects don't need per-project edits. Only GET/POST are allowed at the CORS layer — consistent with the read-public / token-guarded-write model.

snippets.title: One middleware guards every write
snippets.feature: Public reads, token-gated mutations
snippets.explanation: The auth gate for a public demo. The news/digest pages are public content, but ANY mutation (set priority, change topic, edit config, run Discover) flows through this one middleware: if TUBESCOUT_PAGE_TOKEN is set, the request must carry it via ?token= or the X-TubeScout-Token header. When the token is unset (local single-user mode) writes are open. Centralizing it means every current and future write endpoint is protected without per-route code.

snippets.title: Rendering the news feed
snippets.feature: The news page — cards joined across 3 tables
snippets.code:
q = f"""
    SELECT v.video_id, v.url, v.published_at, v.thumbnail, {dup_count},
           COALESCE(s.headline, v.title) AS headline, s.news_card, s.engine,
           c.title AS channel, c.topic, c.priority, c.favorite
    FROM videos v
    JOIN channels c ON v.channel_id = c.channel_id
    LEFT JOIN summaries s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
    WHERE s.video_id IS NOT NULL{dup_filter} AND c.priority != 'mute' AND c.disabled = 0
"""
# favorites float up, then newest-first
q += " ORDER BY c.favorite DESC, v.published_at DESC LIMIT ?"
snippets.explanation: The query behind every card: videos joined to their channel and (left) to their summary. It only shows videos that HAVE a summary, hides duplicates unless ?show=all, and excludes muted/disabled channels. Favorites float to the top, then newest-first. COALESCE(s.headline, v.title) means a card still has a headline even if summarization is mid-flight.

snippets.title: Discovering new uploads
snippets.feature: Twice-daily sweep across active channels
snippets.explanation: The heart of the 07:00/19:00 job. It opens a sweeps run row, walks the active (subscribed + enabled + non-muted) channels favorites-first, and inserts uploads newer than the lookback cutoff. A playlistNotFound error means the channel is dead, so its playlist is set to '' (not NULL) which stops pull-subs from re-backfilling it forever. The last real run discovered 364 new videos across 811 channels.

snippets.title: Overlapping lookback window
snippets.feature: Two daily windows that never miss an upload
snippets.code:
lookback_h = cfg.get("sweep.lookback_hours", 14)
max_per = cfg.get("sweep.max_videos_per_channel", 10)
since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=lookback_h)
snippets.explanation: Sweeps run at 07:00 and 19:00 — 12 hours apart — but each looks back 14 hours. The 2-hour overlap guarantees that an upload published right around a window boundary is still caught by the next sweep, so nothing slips through the cracks. All three knobs are config-driven.

snippets.title: Two-pass topic classification
snippets.feature: Auto-organize channels into topics
snippets.code:
for r in rows:  # only channels with topic_manual = 0
    kw = organizer.classify(r["title"], r["description"], topics_cfg)
    cat = best_category_topic(cats_map.get(r["channel_id"], []))
    # Keyword and YouTube category compete — pick the most specific (highest rank).
    candidates = [t for t in (kw if kw != "other" else None, cat) if t]
    topic = max(candidates, key=lambda t: TOPIC_RANK.get(t, 0)) if candidates else "other"
    db.set_channel_topic(conn, r["channel_id"], topic)
snippets.explanation: Classification runs the keyword heuristic AND YouTube's own topicCategories, then picks the most specific bucket via TOPIC_RANK (ai_ml/software_dev=10 … lifestyle=1) — so a channel tagged [Lifestyle, Science] lands in science, not the lifestyle catch-all. Channels you re-categorized by hand (topic_manual=1) are excluded entirely. This pass cut the 'other' pile from ~450 to ~3.

snippets.title: Captions vs. block — two different outcomes
snippets.feature: Fetch captions without ever crashing
snippets.code:
api = YouTubeTranscriptApi()
try:
    fetched = api.fetch(video_id, languages=languages)
except Exception as e:
    name, msg = type(e).__name__, str(e)
    if name in _SKIP_REASONS:        # TranscriptsDisabled / NoTranscriptFound / ...
        return None                  # no captions — skip quietly, not an error
    if name in ("RequestBlocked", "IpBlocked") or any(m in msg for m in _BLOCK_MARKERS):
        raise IPBlocked(msg)         # YouTube is throttling us — abort the run
    raise
text = " ".join(sn.text for sn in fetched.snippets).strip()
return (getattr(fetched, "language_code", languages[0]), text) if text else None
snippets.explanation: The fetcher distinguishes two failure classes that look similar but mean opposite things. 'No captions available' returns None — a normal outcome marked transcript_status='none'. 'YouTube is blocking your IP' raises IPBlocked, which the caller turns into a cooldown. Everything else re-raises. This is why the caption stage can run unattended twice a day without ever taking down the page.

snippets.title: IP-block backoff via the state table
snippets.feature: Back off for hours instead of hammering
snippets.explanation: When YouTube blocks the scraper, hammering it only extends the block. So on IPBlocked the runner records a future timestamp (transcripts_blocked_until) in the persistent state table and stops; the next cycle sees the cooldown is still active and skips the transcript stage entirely. Favorites/must-reads are fetched first, so the limited transcript budget is spent on what matters most.

snippets.title: The NEXUS /synthesize call
snippets.feature: Summarize a video via the QI AI backbone
snippets.explanation: TubeScout runs no model itself — this is the single bridge to NEXUS. It POSTs to /synthesize pinned to a fast provider chain (Groq→Cloudflare→Gemini), asking for one parallel pass. Crucially it returns None on any failure — NEXUS down, all-providers-rate-limited, or the 'no successful responses' sentinel — which lets the caller fall back to the description so the page never empties.

snippets.title: Summarize-or-fallback per video
snippets.feature: News card from transcript, else description
snippets.explanation: Summaries are decoupled from transcripts: it uses the transcript when one exists, otherwise the video description. NEXUS produces a HEADLINE + 2–4 sentence card; if NEXUS is unavailable it falls back to a trimmed description. The engine column ('nexus' vs 'fallback') records which path was taken — currently 2,374 NEXUS-written vs 1,640 fallback, the backlog the transcript drainer will upgrade.

snippets.title: Implement-worthiness → QI Brain
snippets.feature: Log build-worthy videos to the ecosystem
snippets.code:
base = cfg.get("integration.brain_base", "http://127.0.0.1:9011")
r = httpx.post(f"{base}/api/log_feature", json={
    "source_project": "tubescout",
    "name": (video.get("headline") or video.get("title") or "")[:160],
    "description": f"[score {score:.0f}/10] {rationale}\nTags: {tags}\nVideo: {video.get('url')}",
    "domain": "ai/youtube-scout",
    "code_ref": video.get("url"),
}, timeout=20)  # agent_id omitted -> Brain default 'claude' (FK-valid)
r.raise_for_status()
return True
snippets.explanation: For ai_ml/software_dev videos, NEXUS rates 0–10 how worth-IMPLEMENTING the content is for Renne's own stack (SCORE/TAGS/RATIONALE). Anything ≥ the threshold (default 7.0) is POSTed to the QI Brain's pending-features queue — so a technique demoed on YouTube becomes a candidate the whole ecosystem can decide to adopt. 439 videos scored so far.

snippets.title: Conservative cross-channel dedup
snippets.feature: "+N also covered" — show a story once
snippets.explanation: Headlines are tokenized (stopwords + short words dropped) and clustered by Jaccard overlap ≥ threshold (0.55) within a 72h window. The first video in a cluster is canonical and gets dup_count; the rest get dup_of and are hidden by default, surfaced as '+N also covered'. It is intentionally strict and time-bounded — a false merge that hides a distinct story is worse than missing a near-duplicate.

snippets.title: Local taste profile (never leaves the machine)
snippets.feature: Private discovery without YouTube's ad profile
snippets.code:
favs = [r["title"] for r in conn.execute(
    "SELECT title FROM channels WHERE favorite=1 AND subscribed=1 LIMIT 25").fetchall()]
musts = [r["title"] for r in conn.execute(
    "SELECT title FROM channels WHERE priority='must_read' AND subscribed=1 LIMIT 25").fetchall()]
seed = favs + musts
if len(seed) < 6:  # not enough signal — fall back to AI/tech + biggest topics
    seed += [r["title"] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT title FROM channels WHERE topic IN ('ai','ai_ml','software_dev') ...").fetchall()]
tags = []
for r in conn.execute("SELECT tags FROM scores WHERE implement_score>=7 LIMIT 40").fetchall():
    tags += [t.strip() for t in (r["tags"] or "").split(",") if t.strip()]
return {"seed_channels": ..., "topics": ..., "tags": top_tags}
snippets.explanation: The recommender's taste profile is assembled entirely from your own local data — favorited channels, must-reads, AI/tech channels, and the tags of your highest implement-scored videos — and never sent to YouTube. A NEXUS provider (Groq default, fully-local gemma4 switchable in Settings) reasons over it to suggest channels; YouTube is touched only for a neutral name→channel lookup that reveals nothing about you.

snippets.title: Interests config (editable in-app)
snippets.feature: Renne's watch interests steer the recommender
snippets.explanation: The single config file. The interests list (AI, Travel, Retirement, DOAC) is editable in the UI at Settings → Your interests and steers the Discover recommender. Everything operational — sweep times, the implement-score threshold, dedup strictness, the NEXUS provider chain, integration URLs — lives here too, so tuning the pipeline never needs a code change or restart.

snippets.title: Editing interests from the Settings tab
snippets.feature: Settings → Your interests writes back to config
snippets.explanation: The Settings tab posts only whitelisted keys (_EDITABLE), each coerced to the right type — comma strings become lists, so typing 'AI, Travel, Retirement, DOAC' updates the interests array. set_values walks the dotted path, writes the change back to config/tubescout.json, and reloads the cache, so the next sweep picks it up with no restart.

snippets.title: The fault-tolerant cycle
snippets.feature: One stage failing never aborts the run
snippets.code:
def _safe(label, fn, *a, **k):
    try:
        r = fn(*a, **k); log.info("%s: %s", label, r); return r
    except Exception as e:
        log.error("%s FAILED: %s", label, e); return None

_safe("sweep", sweep.run_sweep)
_safe("reclassify", reclassify.reclassify, conn)
_safe("transcripts", transcripts.process_pending, conn, tcap)
_safe("summarize", summarize.process_pending, conn, 500)
_safe("dedup", dedup.run_dedup, conn)
_safe("score", score.process_pending, conn, 100)
_safe("scout_refresh", scout_feed.import_to_scout, conn)
snippets.explanation: The 07:00/19:00 job (QI_TubeScout_AM/_PM) runs all six pipeline stages plus the Kaze/Scout refresh through _safe(), which catches and logs any stage's exception and returns None. So a YouTube hiccup in the sweep, a NEXUS outage during summarize, or a Brain timeout in score degrades to a logged error — the remaining stages still run and the page stays current.
